difficultyReason: Single causal inference with one visible alternative explanation. Correct answer rules out the alternative — that seasonal weather caused the crop yield increase — by confirming the fertilizer was responsible.
stimulus: A new fertilizer was introduced in Plainville last year, and crop yields increased by 25 percent that season. Farmers are attributing the improved yields to the fertilizer.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that the fertilizer caused the yield increase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Farmers in neighboring towns who did not use the new fertilizer experienced no significant increase in crop yields last year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new fertilizer is less expensive than other fertilizers currently on the market.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Weather conditions in Plainville last year were typical for the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crop yields in Plainville have been declining steadily for the past decade.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The new fertilizer has been tested on vegetables as well as grains.

explanations.correct: If neighboring farmers without the new fertilizer saw no yield increase, this rules out a shared alternative explanation (regional weather or market factors) and strengthens the causal claim that the fertilizer itself was responsible for Plainville's improvement.
explanations.B: Irrelevant — cost does not address the causal claim.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — typical weather would not explain a 25% increase, so this does not strengthen the fertilizer hypothesis.
explanations.D: Does not address last year's causal question; also potentially weakens by suggesting other factors may be at play.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the fact that fertilizer works on vegetables does not address the causal question for grains in Plainville.

difficultyReason: Single causal inference: increased reading comprehension scores at the school with the new program imply the program caused the gains. One obvious alternative: students' prior ability improved independently. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
stimulus: Lincoln High School implemented a new reading intervention program this year. Students' reading comprehension scores increased by an average of 15 percent compared to last year. The school administrator concludes that the program was responsible for the improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the administrator's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reading comprehension scores of students at other schools in the district remained essentially unchanged this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new reading program was adapted from a program that had been successful at a different school.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some students at Lincoln High School did not fully participate in the reading program.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reading comprehension is more important to academic success than other language skills.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teachers at Lincoln High School were given additional professional development in reading instruction.

explanations.correct: If reading comprehension scores at other schools remained unchanged, this rules out the alternative that district-wide or regional factors caused the improvement at Lincoln, strengthening the claim that the program itself was responsible.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — the program's pedigree does not prove it caused this year's gains at Lincoln.
explanations.C: Weakens rather than strengthens — incomplete participation would reduce the program's effect.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the importance of reading comprehension does not address causation.
explanations.E: Introduces a confounding variable; the professional development (not the program itself) might have caused the improvement, thus weakening rather than strengthening.

difficultyReason: Causal claim: price increase caused a drop in coffee sales. Alternative explanation: consumer preference shifted. Correct answer rules out the alternative by confirming consumers still want coffee.
stimulus: A coffee shop raised the price of its coffee by 20 percent last month, and sales volume dropped by 30 percent. The owner concludes that the price increase caused the decline in sales.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the owner's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A new competing coffee shop opened nearby just before the price increase.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Other coffee shops in the area did not raise their prices last month.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average customer at the shop purchases coffee five days a week.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The quality of the coffee remained the same after the price increase.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coffee sales in the city overall increased slightly last month.

explanations.correct: If competing shops did not raise prices, their prices are now relatively lower. Customers switching to competitors due to relative price is consistent with price sensitivity — it directly supports the price-caused-the-decline claim.
explanations.A: Introduces a confounding variable — competition might have caused the sales drop, not the price increase.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — purchase frequency does not explain why customers stopped buying at a higher price.
explanations.D: Rules out quality decline as an alternative, which is helpful; but B is stronger because it shows customers had lower-priced alternatives.
explanations.E: Contradicts the owner's claim — if city sales rose but this shop's fell, something other than market demand (like price) was the cause, but this fact alone doesn't strengthen the owner's specific conclusion relative to alternatives.

difficultyReason: Causal inference: a new medication caused a reduction in headache symptoms. Alternative: placebo effect or regression to the mean. Correct answer rules out placebo by confirming blind trial or mechanism.
stimulus: In a clinical trial, patients who took a new migraine medication reported a 40 percent reduction in headache frequency over three months. Researchers conclude that the medication directly caused this improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients in a control group who received a placebo reported no significant reduction in headache frequency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new migraine medication is easier to take than existing migraine treatments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some patients discontinued use of the medication due to minor side effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Migraines are a common condition affecting millions of people worldwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Previous studies have shown that stress reduction can lower migraine frequency.

explanations.correct: A placebo-controlled comparison directly addresses the alternative explanation of placebo effect. If the control group showed no improvement while the treatment group did, this strengthens the causal claim that the medication (not just patient expectation) caused the improvement.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — ease of use does not prove efficacy or causation.
explanations.C: Weakens rather than strengthens — dropout due to side effects complicates the causal narrative.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — prevalence of migraines does not address causation in this trial.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative explanation: stress reduction (not the medication) might have caused the improvement, thus weakening the claim.

difficultyReason: Predictive causal claim: new environmental regulation will reduce pollution. Alternative: regulation won't be enforced or industry will adapt. Correct answer confirms either enforcement or effectiveness.
stimulus: City officials have enacted strict new emissions limits on industrial manufacturing facilities. Environmental advocates predict that these regulations will lead to a measurable reduction in air pollution levels within two years.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the environmental advocates' prediction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city has hired additional inspectors to monitor compliance with the new emissions limits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some manufacturing facilities in the city may relocate to other states.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Current pollution levels in the city exceed federal air quality standards.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Citizens have expressed strong support for environmental regulations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Industrial emissions account for only a portion of the city's total air pollution.

explanations.correct: Additional inspectors strengthen the claim by addressing a key unstated assumption: that regulations will be actively enforced. Enforcement capability directly supports the prediction that the regulations will produce the expected improvement.
explanations.B: Weakens — if facilities relocate, compliance may be easier (no actual pollution reduction) or the economic base is harmed; either way, uncertainty about effectiveness.
explanations.C: Relevant background but does not strengthen the prediction; we already know pollution is a problem.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — public support does not ensure the regulations will reduce pollution.
explanations.E: Weakens — if industrial emissions are only part of the problem, regulations on industry alone may not achieve measurable overall reduction.

difficultyReason: Causal claim: a technology caused a change in user behavior. Alternative: users already wanted this behavior change. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
stimulus: Since the introduction of mobile payment applications, cash transactions have declined sharply in urban areas. Mobile payment providers attribute this trend to the convenience of their technology.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the mobile payment providers' claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In rural areas without widespread access to mobile payment technology, cash transactions have remained stable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some consumers prefer the security features of mobile payment systems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mobile payment applications offer rewards and incentives to users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Banks have also reduced the number of automated teller machines in urban areas.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mobile payment technology was developed by several competing companies.

explanations.correct: Geographic comparison: rural areas without the technology show stable cash use, while urban areas with it show sharp decline. This rules out the alternative that consumer preferences shifted across the board, and supports the claim that the technology itself drove the change.
explanations.B: Accurate but does not address causation; security preference could have existed before the technology.
explanations.C: Accurate but does not address causation; incentives are a feature, not proof that convenience (not incentives) drove the change.
explanations.D: Introduces a confounding variable — ATM reduction might have caused the cash decline.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the number of competing companies does not address the causal mechanism.

difficultyReason: Causal inference: early language exposure caused higher proficiency. Alternative: genetics or family background. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
stimulus: Children who began learning a second language before age five demonstrate higher proficiency in that language by age ten compared to children who started learning it at age seven. Linguists attribute this difference to the cognitive advantages of early language exposure.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the linguists' explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children from bilingual families who began learning their second language after age seven eventually achieve the same proficiency as children who started earlier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The second language was taught using the same curriculum and methods to both age groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children who learn a second language early also tend to have larger overall vocabularies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Language proficiency is important for academic success in bilingual schools.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some children who started learning a second language before age five did not achieve high proficiency.

explanations.correct: By confirming that both groups received identical instruction, this rules out the alternative that differences in teaching quality or method caused the proficiency gap, and strengthens the claim that early exposure itself (a cognitive advantage) was the causal factor.
explanations.A: Contradicts the empirical observation and thus weakens the argument.
explanations.C: Consistent with the early-exposure hypothesis but does not rule out confounding variables (e.g., family background).
explanations.D: Irrelevant — importance of proficiency does not address causation.
explanations.E: Weakens — exceptions suggest early exposure alone is not sufficient, casting doubt on the causal claim.

difficultyReason: Causal claim: a policy change caused an outcome. Alternative: some other factor was responsible. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
stimulus: After implementing mandatory ethics training for all employees, a corporation reported a 35 percent decrease in workplace misconduct complaints. Management credits the ethics training with this improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens management's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Comparable corporations that did not implement ethics training continued to receive similar levels of misconduct complaints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ethics training program has been accredited by a professional organization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Employees who completed the ethics training reported feeling more confident in their roles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Workplace misconduct includes violations of both company policy and legal standards.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some employees did not attend all sessions of the mandatory ethics training.

explanations.correct: If comparable corporations without the training saw no decrease, this rules out the alternative that industry-wide or economic factors reduced complaints, and strengthens the claim that the training program itself was responsible.
explanations.B: Relevant to program quality but does not prove it caused the complaint reduction.
explanations.C: Accurate but does not address misconduct reduction; employee confidence does not necessarily translate to lower complaints.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the scope of misconduct definition does not address causation.
explanations.E: Weakens — incomplete participation would reduce the training's effect.

difficultyReason: Analogical strength claim: an artwork's popularity indicates its artistic merit. Alternative: popularity reflects marketing, not merit. Correct answer confirms the link.
stimulus: Art critics have long debated whether popular works of art possess genuine artistic merit. A recent exhibition of classical paintings that are widely appreciated by the public has received praise from professional art critics as well. This suggests that popularity and artistic merit often align.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens this conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The exhibition received significant promotional marketing and media attention.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many unpopular paintings in museums have also been praised by professional art critics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Professional art critics have varying opinions about what constitutes artistic merit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The classical paintings in the exhibition are valued highly by collectors worldwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The general public and professional critics often disagree about contemporary artworks.

explanations.correct: If unpopular paintings also receive critical praise, this demonstrates that critical acclaim is not limited to popular works. Combined with the given data (popular works also receive critical praise), this suggests the alignment is genuine rather than coincidental, strengthening the conclusion that popularity and merit can align.
explanations.A: Weakens — if marketing drove the exhibition's popularity (rather than merit), this undermines the alignment claim.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — disagreement about merit criteria does not address the alignment question.
explanations.D: Consistent with popularity/merit alignment but does not prove the alignment; collector value might be driven by investment, not merit.
explanations.E: Contradicts the alignment claim by suggesting public and critical opinions diverge, especially for contemporary work.

difficultyReason: Causal inference: legal precedent caused a change in judicial practice. Alternative: judges changed their interpretation for other reasons. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
stimulus: A landmark court decision was handed down in State X last year. Since then, judges in State X have applied the new legal standard established by that decision in 80 percent of relevant cases. Legal scholars conclude that the precedent has strongly influenced judicial behavior.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the scholars' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Before the landmark decision, judges in State X applied similar legal standards in fewer than 20 percent of relevant cases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Judges in neighboring states have also increased their application of the new legal standard.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The landmark decision was written by a respected judge with extensive legal experience.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some judges in State X have declined to apply the new legal standard in their decisions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The new legal standard addresses an issue that has been debated for many decades.

explanations.correct: The sharp increase from under 20% to 80% application directly demonstrates that judicial behavior changed after the landmark decision, strengthening the causal claim that the precedent itself (not pre-existing judicial trends) drove the change.
explanations.B: Weakens — if neighboring judges (without the precedent) also increased application, an external factor (not the precedent) may be responsible.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — the judge's credentials do not prove the precedent influenced behavior.
explanations.D: Weakens — exceptions suggest the precedent did not fully drive behavior.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the age of the debate does not address whether the precedent caused the behavioral shift.
